//============================================================================
// COLOR DEFINITIONS
//============================================================================
// All color definitions consolidated here for easy maintenance
// Organized by purpose: Legacy displays, then Layer 10-14 airspace boundaries

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// LEGACY DISPLAY COLORS
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Used for runway-dependent STARs, holds, MVA circles, and legacy boundaries
//FROM ESAA

COLORDEF:MIL:159:159:160
COLORDEF:TEXTLABEL:150:150:150
COLORDEF:DCT:159:159:160
COLORDEF:MVA:225:225:225
COLORDEF:AMA:150:190:200
COLORDEF:AMATEXT:75:110:120
COLORDEF:Coastline:80:80:80
//

COLORDEF:STAR:0:0:168
// Dark blue - STAR waypoints and routes

COLORDEF:APPGray:90:90:90  
// Medium grey - APP area labels and text

COLORDEF:Black:21:21:21
// Near-black - background elements

COLORDEF:Blue:24:84:120
// Medium blue - primary route color

COLORDEF:RNAV-Z:126:126:126
// Light grey - RNAV-Z approaches

COLORDEF:RNPAR:0:85:0
// Dark green - RNAV approaches with specific requirements

COLORDEF:APCH:164:164:0
// Yellow - approach waypoints and transitions

COLORDEF:RED:255:0:0
// Bright red - holds and critical elements

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// LAYER 10-14 AIRSPACE BOUNDARY COLORS  
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Grey-scale hierarchy: Darker = your responsibility, Lighter = not yours
// Design principle: Subtle awareness without visual clutter

COLORDEF:SECTOR_BASE:28:28:28
// Darkest grey - Your controlled airspace (active sector boundary)
// Rarely displayed - mostly overwritten by delegation layers

COLORDEF:UNCONTROLLED:42:42:42
// Dark grey with sparse fill - Class G airspace (no ATC service)
// Examples: CHARLO-NO-CONTROL, northern Labrador beyond MTCA
// Used with COORDPOLY:100 for subtle sparse dot pattern

COLORDEF:DELEGATION:53:60:60
// Medium grey - Areas delegated to subordinate positions
// APP/TWR/sector boundaries when those positions are online
// Solid fill (COORDPOLY:0) shows "carved out" from your responsibility

COLORDEF:QM_QX_SPLIT:105:105:105
// Slightly lighter - Internal FIR boundary between CZQM and CZQX
// Only visible when both center positions online simultaneously

COLORDEF:COLD_NBR:110:110:110
// Light grey - Neighbor FIR boundaries (always visible)
// CZUL/ZBW/BIRD/CZEG - shows boundary exists even when unstaffed
// Subtle presence for situational awareness

COLORDEF:HOT_NBR:140:140:140
// Brighter grey - Neighbor FIR actively staffed
// Overwrites COLD_NBR on Layer 13 when neighbor online
// Visual cue: "Coordinate with live neighbor controller!"

// SECTORIZATION

// CYHZ TCU

//============================================================================
// AIRSPACE BOUNDARIES SECTION - DYNAMIC ACTIVATION
//============================================================================
//
//
// PURPOSE:
// Display airspace boundaries that dynamically appear/disappear based on
// which control positions are staffed online. Helps controllers maintain
// situational awareness of delegation states and responsibilities.
//
// DESIGN PHILOSOPHY:
// - Subtlety: Boundaries inform without overwhelming - aircraft tags remain priority
// - Visual Hierarchy: Lighter shades = "not yours" (uncontrolled/delegated)
// - State Visualization: Same geometry + different colors = operational state changes
// - Non-Translucent Layers: Higher layers completely overwrite lower layers
//
// COLOR STRATEGY (Shades of Grey):
//   
//   SECTOR_BASE (80,80,80)         = Your controlled airspace
//   UNCONTROLLED (95,95,95)         = Class G - no ATC service provided
//   DELEGATION (100,100,100)        = Delegated to APP/TWR (carved from your airspace)
//   QM_QX_SPLIT (105,105,105)      = Internal CZQM/CZQX boundary when both online
//   COLD_NBR (110,110,110)          = Neighbor FIR exists but unstaffed (subtle)
//   HOT_NBR (140,140,140)           = Neighbor FIR actively staffed (coordinate!)
//
// LAYER STRATEGY:
//   Layer 10: Static uncontrolled areas (always visible)
//   Layer 11: Cold neighbor boundaries (always visible, subtle)
//   Layer 12: Internal delegations (APP/TWR/sectors when positions online)
//   Layer 13: Hot neighbors (overwrites Layer 11 when neighbor staffed)
//   Layer 14: CZQM/CZQX split (only when both centers online simultaneously)
//
// NOTE: Layers 10-14 chosen to avoid conflict with existing content:
//   - Runway-dependent STAR displays use default layers
//   - MVA circles use default layers
//   - Existing APP boundaries (CYHZ APP, CYZX APP) use default layers
//
// REFERENCE DOCUMENTS:
//   - NAV CANADA Designated Airspace Handbook (DAH) - Effective 0901Z 7 AUG 2025
//   - CZQM FIR Centre Airspace Manual v2 draft 3
//   - Low-Level IFR Charts: LO_07 (Goose area), LO_08 (North)
//   - ESE Sector File: CZQQ-DO-NOT-USE_20251107023304-251101-0017.ese
//
//============================================================================

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// COLOR DEFINITIONS FOR AIRSPACE BOUNDARIES
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Using unique names to avoid conflicts with existing colors
// (Blue, APPGray, Black, STAR, RNAV-Z, RNPAR, APCH, RED already defined above)

//============================================================================
// LAYER 12: INTERNAL DELEGATIONS - TWR, APP, AND SECTORS
//============================================================================
// These boundaries activate when specific positions log on
// APP, TWR, and sector areas are "carved out" from center airspace
// Display in DELEGATION color (medium grey) to show "not your responsibility"

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// TOWER (TWR) BOUNDARIES - Class D Airspace
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// All tower areas are Class D airspace from surface to specified ceiling
// Controllers provide separation services to all IFR and VFR aircraft
// 
// Using COORD_CIRCLE for clean, efficient definitions:
//   - One line defines entire circle vs 60+ coordinate points
//   - Spacing parameter (degrees) controls polygon smoothness
//   - 10° spacing adequate for circles under 20 NM radius
//
// STANDARD RADII (from CZQM FIR Centre Airspace Manual):
//   7 NM:  Standard Class D radius (CYHZ, CYFC, CYQM, CYZX, CYQX, CYYT)
//   10 NM: CYYR - Larger for military MTCA operations
//   5 NM:  LFVP - Smaller, French territorial delegation
//
// ACTIVATION:
// Each TWR activates when its respective position logs on
// Position IDs from ESE [POSITIONS] section
//
// SYNTAX PATTERN:
//	LAYER:12 
//   MAP:AirportCode_TWR
//   FOLDER:AIRSPACE BOUNDARIES
//   COLOR:DELEGATION
//   ACTIVE:MapID:PositionID
//   COORD_CIRCLE:AirportCode:RadiusNM:SpacingDegrees
//   COORDPOLY:0
//
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
